title: Web Performance Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Web Performance course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: Why keep test conditions the same?
options: So before-and-after results can be compared fairly
So every result is guaranteed to be zero
exercises.explanation: A performance measurement is a clue about a real task. A slow phone and a fast laptop may get different results from the same page.

exercises.question: Which measure is about unexpected layout movement?
options: LCP
CLS
exercises.explanation: Core Web Vitals describe loading, response to input and visual stability. Their short names are LCP, INP and CLS.

exercises.question: Why declare image width and height?
options: To reserve space and reduce layout jumps
To force every image to download twice
exercises.explanation: Image width and height tell the browser the picture's shape before it finishes loading. That lets the browser keep the right amount of space.

exercises.question: Which image is usually a poor lazy-loading choice?
options: A photo far below the first screen
The main image visible immediately on page load
exercises.explanation: Lazy loading delays some images until they are near the visible area. This can save early work for a long page.

exercises.question: What does srcset offer the browser?
options: Image file choices with their sizes
A list of text colours
exercises.explanation: Responsive image sources let the browser choose a suitable image size. A small screen should not always need the largest file.

exercises.question: What does defer allow during the download?
options: Every script runs before any HTML exists
HTML parsing can continue
exercises.explanation: A deferred classic script downloads while HTML is read and runs after parsing. This can let the browser build the page sooner.

exercises.question: When is chart.js first requested here?
options: When the button is clicked
Only when the user closes the page
exercises.explanation: Dynamic import can load a JavaScript module when a feature is used. It can keep optional work out of the first page load.

exercises.question: Why group the width reads before style writes?
options: To stop all CSS from loading
To avoid unnecessary repeated layout calculations
exercises.explanation: Reading layout after each style change can make the browser repeatedly calculate positions. Group reads and then writes when possible.

exercises.question: What kind of job suits requestAnimationFrame?
options: A page visual update
A guarantee to run every exact millisecond
exercises.explanation: requestAnimationFrame asks the browser to run a visual update before a future paint. It is useful when combining several changes for one frame.

exercises.question: What does the fallback font help avoid?
options: Every kind of network request
Invisible words while the custom font loads
exercises.explanation: A fallback font shows readable words while a web font loads. font-display: swap lets text appear using that fallback.

exercises.question: Why are long cache times useful for versioned assets?
options: The address changes when the contents change
The browser can never reuse them
exercises.explanation: A cache keeps a response so it may be reused. Cache headers tell the browser how long a response can stay fresh.

exercises.question: What makes a performance check useful over time?
options: Running it once and never looking again
Repeating it under clear conditions after changes
exercises.explanation: A useful performance budget sets limits that matter for the page. Recheck after changes so a fast page does not slowly become heavy.
